newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Dec 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Dec 16.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Fidel Ramos reports back to work today after a viral infection and may risk a relapse with a full schedule that will take him out of the Presidential Palace three times. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- Starting today, taxi cab fares rise by 4 pesos following the approval of the Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board. (MANILA STANDARD)

- Vice-president Joseph Estrada brands a group seeking Constitutional amendment and therefore an extension of President Ramos' term as "nothing but a rag-tag band of aging constitutional vandals." (MANILA CHRONICLE)

- The Metro Manila Development Authority grants provisional exemption starting today to all public utility vehicles from the once-a-week restrictions so that people have adequate transport facilities during the Christmas rush. Vehicle use has been restricted by the government in Manila in a bid to tackle the severe traffic congestion problem. (BULLETIN)
- The Japanese government agrees to slash from 35 percent to a mere one percent the loan loss provision rules for Japanese banks that have lent to Philippine banks. (TODAY)

- The Japanese government may trim down its allocation to official development assistance (ODA) programme intended for recipient countries in the region, including the Philippines, Japanese Embassy first secretary Reiichiro Takahashi said. (MANILA CHRONICLE)

- The state-run National Power Corp may cut in half the expected seven to eight centavo increase in power rates this month following a 26-centavo per litre reduction in the price of fuel oil. (MANILA BULLETIN)

- The Department of Trade and Industry prepares to start public hearings on the tariffs on information technology products for the early reduction of these rates as proposed by the United States during the World Trade Organisation (WTO) meeting.
- The Securities and Exchange Commission grants today self-regulatory status to the Philippine Stock Exchange (MANILA TIMES/INQUIRER)

- The Philippines' growing current account deficit is not worrisome as continued strong inflows from investments and remittances from overseas Filipino workers are enough to finance it. (PHILIPPINE STAR)

- Congress will not be able to act on the proposed Intellectual Property Rights Code and will instead concentrate on the proposed 1997 budget before adjourning this week for the Christmas break. (BUSINESSWORLD)
